issues.description: Method return type mismatch for Animal.messageOnFeed(): the problem statement (UML and textual tasks) declares abstract method Animal.messageOnFeed() returning String, while the solution repository's Animal.java declares public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed(). This inconsistency means students reading the spec expect to implement/override a String-returning method, but the provided solution API uses a different type (FeedResponse), causing confusion and preventing a consistent implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix (preserve exercise intent): change the solution API so Animal.messageOnFeed() returns String. Modify solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java to declare public abstract String messageOnFeed(); and update all concrete subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return String values. Remove or repurpose FeedResponse (e.g., delete class or keep for alternative tasks) and update Farm.feedAllAnimals() and singFarmSongVerse() to treat messageOnFeed() as a String. Alternative (less preferred): update problem statement and UML to specify FeedResponse and document its semantics, then update all templates and tests to expect FeedResponse consistently.

issues.description: Internal solution repository mismatch for messageOnFeed(): Animal.java declares public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed(), but Goat.java implements public String messageOnFeed(). This signature mismatch will cause compilation errors in the solution and prevents students from using the provided solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure all concrete subclasses match the abstract method signature. Preferred fix (consistent with problem statement): change Animal.messageOnFeed() to return String and update Pig.java and Seal.java to return String (replace FeedResponse instances with the raw message strings). Then change Goat.messageOnFeed() remains as String (no change). If choosing to keep FeedResponse, change Goat.messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse instance (e.g., return new FeedResponse("Maah!", true);) and update Goat.java signature accordingly. The simplest resolution is to standardize on String across Animal and all subclasses to match the exercise description.

issues.description: Concept: the animal feeding message. Problem statement & UML declare Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String (UML: messageOnFeed():String) and the Farm song implementation in the problem expects to print the String returned by messageOnFeed(). Template Farm.singFarmSongVerse() prints feed messages as plain Strings. In the solution repository, the abstract method Animal.messageOnFeed() has been changed to return a FeedResponse object (class FeedResponse), and a new type FeedResponse is introduced. Additionally, the solution's Goat class still implements messageOnFeed() returning String (not FeedResponse), creating an internal type mismatch in the solution. This divergence between the problem (String), the template (expects String), and the solution (FeedResponse) breaks the one-to-one mapping students require and will confuse or block them: they cannot tell whether to implement messageOnFeed() to return String or FeedResponse, and the solution as provided is inconsistent/compilable only if corrected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the messageOnFeed() contract consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix (A): change the solution to match the problem and template by having Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (remove or refactor FeedResponse), and update all concrete animal classes (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return String messages (e.g., "Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"). Ensure Farm.feedAllAnimals() and singFarmSongVerse() call and print the returned String. Alternative fix (B): if FeedResponse is intentionally required, update the problem statement, UML and template to document FeedResponse as the return type (describe its fields and toString() behavior) and update template Farm and all example code to extract/print the message field consistently. Prefer option (A) to align with the current exercise description and reduce student confusion.
